cleanIntro: The 692 is the seven-shot Taurus with two cylinders - one for .357 Magnum and .38 Special, one for 9mm Luger on stellar clips - and the cylinder swap is the ONLY disassembly Taurus publishes for it. Everything else is a cylinder-open clean: the book says the revolver is cleaned and lubricated without any disassembly and instructs that the barrel is not to be taken apart. It also has a fully adjustable rear sight, so there is something on the topstrap worth protecting.

steps.title: One 692, two cylinders, three barrel lengths
steps.action: Confirm what you have: the 692 is DA/SA, seven rounds, chambered .357 Magnum / .38 Special / 9mm Luger, on a 6 1/2, 3 or 2 1/2 inch barrel, with a fixed front sight and a fully adjustable rear. The 9mm capability is not a second chambering in one cylinder - it is a second cylinder, used with stellar clips.
steps.prose: This is the fact that governs the whole session. A 692 on the bench may be wearing either cylinder, and which one it is wearing changes what you clear, how you unload, and what you brush. Establish it before you touch the thumb piece rather than discovering it when the cases will not eject.
steps.aside: Taurus permits one substitution in this family: .38 Special ammunition may be fired in any of their revolvers chambered for .357 Magnum, and they state these are the only caliber substitutions that will function.
steps.cite:
692
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 6 — Specifications, printed p.13 (PDF p.7)

steps.title: Thumb piece forward, cylinder out, seven chambers checked
steps.action: Muzzle safe and finger off the trigger. Push the thumb piece forward with your right thumb, press the cylinder out to the left, and visually check all seven chambers.
steps.prose: Forward, not down - the Taurus latch slides toward the muzzle and pushing it any other way simply clamps the cylinder shut. Seven is the count; a habit built on a six-shooter stops one chamber early, and on a 692 fitted with the 9mm cylinder a rimless case sits low enough that the last chamber is the easiest one to misread.
steps.quote: Revolver Be sure the firearm is completely unloaded and contains no cartridges or cartridge cases. With the thumb of the right hand push the thumb piece forward. Then press on the cylinder to swing it to the left. Visually check that all seven (7) chambers are empty.
steps.cite:
692
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 6 — Firearms Safety Systems, printed p.9 (PDF p.5)

steps.title: Muzzle up, push sharply - and collect the stellar clip if one is in there
steps.action: Elevate the muzzle with the cylinder fully out and press sharply on the extractor rod. With the .357/.38 cylinder the cases drop free; with the 9mm cylinder the seven cases come out AS A UNIT on the stellar clip, and the clip must be collected rather than left in the cylinder.
steps.prose: That difference is the practical heart of owning a 692. A stellar clip left behind in a chamber recess stops the next cylinder-load seating, and a clip that has been bent by being levered out will hold cases out of alignment. Taurus's own instruction is explicit about collecting it once the rounds are ejected.
steps.quote: Cartridges are then ejected by pressing sharply on the extractor rod. The cylinder is now ready to be reloaded. Make sure to collect the stellar clip once you have ejected the rounds.
steps.cite:
692
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 6 — Operating Instructions, printed p.20 (PDF p.11)
steps.warn: Spent cases will be hot and may have sharp edges. Exercise caution when removing the cases or injury may occur.

steps.title: The cylinder swap - the one disassembly this book publishes
steps.action: With the revolver unloaded and the muzzle in a safe direction, swing the cylinder fully out, press the cylinder release button on the RIGHT side of the frame, and slide the cylinder assembly forward off the crane. Reverse the process to fit the other cylinder, and push it forward at the end to confirm it is secure.
steps.prose: Two controls, two different sides: the thumb piece is on the left and opens the cylinder, the cylinder release button is on the right and frees the cylinder from the crane. People reach for the left-side latch a second time and conclude the assembly is seized. Do this over a mat - the cylinder assembly comes off in your hand with nothing holding it once the button is pressed, and a dropped .357 cylinder can be knocked out of true.
steps.quote: Holding the unloaded firearm with the muzzle pointing in a safe direction, and the cylinder in its outermost position, press on the cylinder release button on the right side (Fig. 1) of the frame and slide the cylinder assembly forward (Fig. 2 & Fig.3). Reverse this process to engage the other cylinder. Once the other cylinder is installed, ensure it is secure in place by pushing it forward.
steps.cite:
692
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 6 — Swapping the Cylinder, printed p.22 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: Cylinder out, every chamber looked into and felt
steps.action: Before any solvent: muzzle safe, finger off the trigger, thumb piece depressed and the cylinder completely swung out, and the revolver confirmed unloaded by looking into and feeling each chamber.
steps.prose: Do it again after a cylinder swap as well as before it - swapping cylinders is exactly the moment a round from the other cylinder ends up loose on the bench and then back in a chamber. Both senses: a case head deep in a .357 chamber is nearly invisible and unmistakable to a fingertip.
steps.quote: Before cleaning, (1) keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, (2) keep your finger off the trigger, (3) depress thumb piece and completely swing out the cylinder, (4) ensure the firearm is completely unloaded by looking and feeling each chamber.
steps.cite:
692
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 6 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.25 (PDF p.13)

steps.title: The adjustable rear sight is yours - the section applies, so protect it
steps.action: The 692's rear sight is listed as fully adjustable, so this book's 'External Adjustable Sight Models Only' procedure genuinely describes your revolver: elevation screw counterclockwise to raise, clockwise to lower, windage screw clockwise to move the notch right. Note the setting before you clean around it.
steps.prose: That heading is a scope statement and it is doing real work in this book - Taurus prints the same paragraph in manuals covering fixed-sight revolvers where it applies to nobody. Here it applies, which means a cloth dragged across the topstrap can shift a zero without a sound. Adjust at the range against a target, never at the cleaning bench.
steps.quote: External Adjustable Sight Models Only To adjust, make sure the firearm is unloaded and always keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction. If possible, leave the cylinder open during adjustment.
steps.cite:
692
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 6 — Adjusting the Sights, printed p.24 (PDF p.13)

steps.title: This procedure belongs to the 692 and nothing that looks like it
steps.action: Take none of the above onto another revolver. Taurus prints the warning themselves: models which look nearly the same differ widely in design, operation and the location and function of their controls.
steps.prose: The 692's right-side cylinder release is the case in point - almost no other revolver has one, and pressing an equivalent-looking button on a different gun will do something else entirely. If your frame has no button on the right side, the cylinder does not come off and none of the swap step applies.
steps.quote:
FIREARMS ARE NOT ALL ALIKE
Many makes and models of firearms might LOOK nearly the same. However, they differ widely in design, operation, and in the location and function of various controls.
steps.cite:
692
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 6 — Ammunition, printed p.18 (PDF p.10)

steps.title: Two cylinders means two cleaning jobs, not one
steps.action: Clean whichever cylinder is fitted AND the one in the box. Brush all seven chambers of each with solvent and follow with a dry patch, take the carbon ring off both front faces, and clean behind both extractor stars with the rod pushed back.
steps.prose: A stored cylinder is the one that gets forgotten, and 9mm cylinders in particular collect a hard ring at the case mouth because the chambers are stepped for a shorter case. Check the stellar clips at the same time - a bent clip is the most common cause of a 692 that will not close on the 9mm cylinder, and it costs nothing to lay them on a flat surface and look.
steps.quote: 3. In order to keep a gun in perfect condition it must be kept clean and covered with a slight film of good quality oil to prevent corrosion. This is especially necessary after use.
steps.cite:
692
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 6 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.25 (PDF p.13)

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Cylinder swung out, seven chambers empty, and - if you were swapping - the second cylinder on the crane and pushed forward until it is secure. That is the whole of it: Taurus states the firearm is cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly, and instructs that the barrel is not disassembled.
steps.prose: The exploded view is scoped to the 6.5-inch gun and is a parts list, not a sequence - so it is not even a complete picture of the 3 and 2.5 inch variants, let alone an instruction. Where a repair genuinely needs the revolver opened, the book routes it to the factory, a qualified gunsmith or the importer.
steps.quote: 1. The firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly. Do not disassemble the barrel.
steps.cite:
692
INSTRUCTION MANUAL — Rev. 6 — Care and Maintenance, printed p.25 (PDF p.13)

deepAbsentReason: The Taurus 692 book publishes exactly one owner-level disassembly - the cylinder swap - and that is part of the field strip above, not a deeper procedure. Beyond it the book says the firearm may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions without the need of any disassembly and adds 'Do not disassemble the barrel.' Where disassembly is genuinely necessary it routes the revolver to the factory, a qualified gunsmith or the importer. The exploded view is a parts list headed 'EXPLODED VIEW (MODEL 692 - 6.5" BARREL)', scoped to one barrel length and carrying no order of operations. There is nothing deeper published, so nothing deeper is walked.

cleaning.name: BORE, FORCING CONE & PORTS
tasks: Remove all powder residue from the barrel and adjacent areas with an appropriate brush
If lead is detected in the barrel, scrub it with a brass brush drenched with oil, then lubricate
Clean the barrel ports - the 692's ported barrel traps residue in the port cuts where a bore brush never reaches
Work the forcing cone deliberately; it takes the gas cutting from seven fast .357 rounds
Confirm a clear bore against a light

cleaning.name: BOTH CYLINDERS & THE STELLAR CLIPS
tasks: Brush all seven chambers of the fitted cylinder and all seven of the spare, then dry-patch both
Take the carbon ring off the front face of each cylinder
Push each extractor rod back and clean behind the star
Lay every stellar clip on a flat surface and check none is bent - a bent clip holds cases out of line and stops the cylinder closing
Wipe the crane and the cylinder release button on the right of the frame so the swap stays smooth

cleaning.name: SIGHTS, EXTERIOR & STORAGE
tasks: Note the rear sight setting, then wipe around the elevation and windage screws rather than across them
Rub the revolver with a lightly oiled cloth; remove the excess but leave a thin protecting film
Remove dust from all crevices with a small, clean brush
Do not keep the revolver in contact with moisture-attracting or acidic materials, and avoid cloth holsters
Clean before more than 200 rounds go through in a row

reassembly: If the cylinders were swapped, slide the chosen cylinder assembly back onto the crane and push it forward until it is secure in place.
Let the extractor rod return fully, then swing the cylinder closed until it latches - never snap it shut.
Close the cylinder and check the locking by manually turning the cylinder until it stops, as the book instructs after loading.
Confirm the correct cylinder is fitted for the ammunition you intend to carry, and put the other one away with its clips.
fncheck: With all seven chambers confirmed empty: the fitted cylinder must be pushed fully forward and secure on the crane before anything else - a 692 whose cylinder assembly is not seated is not safe to close. The cylinder should latch with light thumb pressure and show no side play; turning it by hand should feel the stop drop into all seven notches; the transfer bar must stay clear of the firing pin until the trigger goes fully through; and both single and double action should reset positively. Check the rear sight screws are where you left them, and if the 9mm cylinder is fitted, confirm a stellar clip seats flat in it before the revolver is loaded.
